**HEADLINE:** Dutch Football Star Anet Smits Makes Surprise Move to Badminton, Earns Spot on WikiProject Focus List

**AMSTERDAM, NETHERLANDS** - In a shocking turn of events, Dutch association football player Anet Smits has announced her decision to trade in her cleats for a badminton racket. The 27-year-old midfielder, known for her lightning-fast speed and agility on the pitch, has been quietly honing her skills on the badminton court and has now earned a spot on the prestigious WikiProject Badminton\/tournament focus list. Smits, who has played for top-tier clubs like Ajax and PSV Eindhoven, revealed that she had been drawn to badminton's fast-paced and strategic nature. "I've always been fascinated by the speed and agility required in badminton," Smits said in an exclusive interview. "As a footballer, I've always prided myself on my quick reflexes and ability to think on my feet. Badminton is a natural fit for me." Smits' decision to switch sports has sent shockwaves through the Dutch football community, with many of her former teammates and coaches expressing surprise and admiration for her bold move. "Anet's always been an exceptional athlete, and I have no doubt she'll excel in badminton," said her former coach, Ronald Koeman. "She's got the dedication and work ethic to succeed in any sport she chooses." According to sources close to the WikiProject Badminton\/tournament focus list, Smits' impressive performance at the recent Dutch Badminton Championships caught the attention of project administrators. Her name was added to the list alongside other top badminton players from around the world, recognizing her potential to make a significant impact on the sport. "We're thrilled to have Anet on board," said WikiProject Badminton administrator, Emily Chen. "Her unique background in football brings a fresh perspective to the sport, and we're excited to see how she'll contribute to the badminton community." Smits is set to make her international badminton debut at the upcoming European Badminton Championships in April. With her inclusion on the WikiProject focus list, fans and enthusiasts alike will be keeping a close eye on her progress. **STATISTICS:**

* Anet Smits' badminton ranking has jumped 50 places in the past month, according to the Badminton World Federation.
